feed.title: NPR Topics: Politics
feed.subtitle: Follow NPR Politics for nonpartisan coverage of government, elections, policy debates and voting rights. Plus weekday audio from The NPR Politics Podcast.

entry.title: AIPAC halts endorsements and direct contributions to candidates
entry.summary: The pro-Israel lobbying group and influential political funder announced it would no longer endorse candidates or give directly to campaigns. AIPAC's affiliated super PAC, though, will continue.

entry.title: The Justice Department begins notifying counties where it wants to monitor elections
entry.summary: The department has long deployed election monitors, but the Trump administration's unprecedented steps to try to wrestle control over elections have led to new concerns about DOJ monitoring this year.

entry.title: California gas prices have long plagued Democratic candidates. This year is different
entry.summary: Gas prices in California continue to be the highest in the nation, but the war in Iran has given California Democrats a rare opportunity to turn the tables on the issue.

entry.title: Vivek Ramaswamy's attack ad features mother of Amy Acton, who alleges childhood abuse
entry.summary: A campaign ad by Republican candidate for Ohio governor Vivek Ramaswamy includes the mother of Democrat Amy Acton. Acton says they've been estranged since she was abused as a child by her stepfather.

entry.title: Poll: Voters want Congress to be a check on Trump, trust Democrats more on issues
entry.summary: A new poll shows record support for Democratic congressional candidates ahead of the midterms, as voters feel the party is better attuned to handling their top issues.

entry.title: Top 2 Democrats on Intel say they're preparing for Trump to claim foreign meddling
entry.summary: The top Democrats on the House and Senate intelligence committees said they are working under the presumption that the president will seek to justify election interference by alleging fraud.

entry.title: How Trump's attacks on voting system integrity might affect upcoming elections
entry.summary: Election law expert Rick Hasen explains Trump's interference in the midterms, including threatening local officials with criminal prosecution unless they strike alleged noncitizens from voter rolls.

entry.title: Why local officials are feeling 'on edge' as election day approaches
entry.summary: Al Schmidt is the chief election official in the state of Pennsylvania. President Trump's insults put him in danger during the 2020 ballot count. Now Schmidt talks about preparing for the midterms.

entry.title: Supreme Court upholds pause on Trump's anti-trans prison policy
entry.summary: The Supreme Court ruled Wednesday that the Trump administration has to continue providing gender-affirming care to inmates in federal prisons as litigation on efforts to change the policy continues.

entry.title: Trump leans into unprecedented power ahead of midterm elections
entry.summary: Less than two weeks before Election Day, President Trump continues to crash through barriers that he wouldn't dare cross in his first term.
